subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: A 74-year-old man has progressive fatigue, pallor, and easy bruising. CBC shows hemoglobin 8.9 g/dL,white blood cell count 2,300/microL with neutropenia, and platelets 78,000/microL; MCV is 102 fL. Bone marrow biopsy is hypercellular with dysplastic maturational abnormalities and 12% blasts.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

options.text: Acute myelogenous leukemia
Aplastic anemia
Myelodysplastic syndrome
Multiple myeloma
Chronic myelogenous leukemia

explanation_correct: Myelodysplastic syndromes are stem cell disorders of ineffective hematopoiesis with maturation defects in nonlymphoid lineages. They produce cytopenias despite a hypercellular, dysplastic marrow, have fewer than 20% marrow blasts, and occur mainly in older adults. These disorders can transform to AML.

explanation_incorrect.A: AML requires more than 20% blasts in the marrow or blood, whereas this patient has only 12% blasts with prominent dysplasia.
explanation_incorrect.B: Aplastic anemia causes pancytopenia but with a hypocellular marrow rather than a hypercellular dysplastic one.
explanation_incorrect.D: Multiple myeloma presents with lytic lesions, an M spike, and rouleaux rather than dysplastic pancytopenia.
explanation_incorrect.E: CML is defined by t(9;22)/BCR-ABL with marked granulocytosis and splenomegaly, not ineffective hematopoiesis with cytopenias.

educationalObjective: MDS causes ineffective hematopoiesis with cytopenias, a hypercellular dysplastic marrow, and fewer than 20% blasts in older adults.

subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: A 68-year-old woman with anemia, neutropenia, and 8% marrow blasts has a peripheral smear showing neutrophils with only two nuclear lobes, producing a bilobed duet appearance rather than the usual three to five lobes.
question: Which of the following best identifies this morphologic finding?

options.text: Howell-Jolly bodies indicating post-splenectomy state
Pseudo-Pelger-Huet anomaly, associated with myelodysplastic syndromes or drugs such as immunosuppressants
Auer rods indicating acute promyelocytic leukemia
Schistocytes indicating microangiopathic hemolysis
Smudge cells indicating chronic lymphocytic leukemia

explanation_correct: Pseudo-Pelger-Huet anomaly describes neutrophils with bilobed duet nuclei. It is associated with myelodysplastic syndromes and can also be caused by drugs such as immunosuppressants. Recognizing it supports a diagnosis of MDS in a patient with unexplained cytopenias and dysplastic marrow changes.

explanation_incorrect.A: Howell-Jolly bodies are retained nuclear remnants within red cells after splenectomy or hyposplenism, not bilobed neutrophil nuclei.
explanation_incorrect.C: Auer rods are myeloperoxidase-positive cytoplasmic inclusions in myeloblasts, most characteristically in acute promyelocytic leukemia.
explanation_incorrect.D: Schistocytes are fragmented erythrocytes produced by microangiopathic hemolysis in TTP, HUS, or DIC, not a neutrophil abnormality.
explanation_incorrect.E: Smudge cells are crushed mature lymphocytes seen in chronic lymphocytic leukemia.

educationalObjective: Bilobed duet neutrophils are the pseudo-Pelger-Huet anomaly, a morphologic clue to MDS or immunosuppressant drug effect.

subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: A 61-year-old man received alkylating chemotherapy and chest radiation for Hodgkin lymphoma 8 years ago. He now has macrocytic anemia, neutropenia, and thrombocytopenia, and bone marrow biopsy shows dysplastic changes with 10% blasts.
question: Which of the following best explains his current hematologic condition?

options.text: Acute promyelocytic leukemia with t(15;17)
Iron deficiency anemia caused by chronic blood loss
Autoimmune destruction of hematopoietic stem cells
Paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria from a PIGA mutation
Therapy-related myelodysplastic syndrome following prior chemotherapy and radiation

explanation_correct: MDS may arise de novo or after environmental exposures such as radiation, benzene, and chemotherapy, including prior alkylating agents. This patient has cytopenias with dysplasia and fewer than 20% blasts, which fits MDS rather than overt leukemia. MDS also carries a risk of transformation to AML.

explanation_incorrect.A: APL with t(15;17) presents with promyelocytes, Auer rods, and often DIC, not with a remote therapy-related dysplastic marrow.
explanation_incorrect.B: Iron deficiency produces microcytic hypochromic anemia, not pancytopenia with marrow dysplasia and blasts.
explanation_incorrect.C: Autoimmune stem cell destruction describes aplastic anemia, which has a hypocellular rather than dysplastic hypercellular marrow.
explanation_incorrect.D: PNH causes complement-mediated intravascular hemolysis and thrombosis due to a PIGA mutation, not dysplastic cytopenias.

educationalObjective: MDS can be de novo or therapy related after radiation, benzene, or chemotherapy exposure and may progress to AML.

subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: A 70-year-old woman with known myelodysplastic syndrome, previously showing 9% marrow blasts, presents with worsening fatigue, neutropenia, and thrombocytopenia. Repeat bone marrow biopsy now shows 28% myeloblasts.
question: Which of the following best describes her current hematologic condition?

options.text: Transformation to acute myelogenous leukemia, defined by more than 20% marrow blasts
Persistent myelodysplastic syndrome, because blasts remain below 30%
Richter transformation into diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
Blast crisis of chronic myelogenous leukemia with BCR-ABL rearrangement
Hairy cell leukemia with dry tap marrow fibrosis

explanation_correct: The defining blast threshold separates MDS, which has fewer than 20% marrow blasts, from AML, which has more than 20%. This patient has progressed from 9% to 28% blasts, so her MDS has transformed to AML, a recognized complication of these stem cell disorders.

explanation_incorrect.B: The diagnostic cutoff is 20%, not 30%; 28% blasts already meets criteria for AML.
explanation_incorrect.C: Richter transformation refers to CLL/SLL converting into an aggressive lymphoma, most often DLBCL, not to MDS progression.
explanation_incorrect.D: CML blast crisis requires the Philadelphia chromosome t(9;22)/BCR-ABL and a preceding chronic phase, which are not described here.
explanation_incorrect.E: Hairy cell leukemia is a mature B-cell tumor with hairlike projections, marrow fibrosis, and a dry tap, not a blast proliferative disorder.

educationalObjective: Transformation from MDS to AML is defined by marrow blasts rising above the 20% threshold.
